thesis: This is a position-management update, not a fresh pitch. DKS was bought 2026-11-13 at 144.50 and closed 2026-11-18 at 144.69, so the trade is flat with its binary event two sessions away. A repeat miss gaps the stock through the 138.18 SMA50 in one session and the 129.00 stop does not protect against a gap below it. counter_argument: Sell-side is moving the wrong way: bullish share fell from 61.3% to 53.1% over four months (strong_buy+buy 15 of 32 at 2026-11-01 vs 19 of 31 at 2026-08-01), and the stock is 40.8% below its 150-day high of 244.38. The bear case is that the insiders bought a falling knife and the de-rating is a demand problem, not a multiple problem. It is answered only partially - the buying was concentrated after the miss, at prices below today, by seven separate people rather than one - which is why conviction is 4 and not 5, and why half comes off before the print.

catalyst.event: A proposed rule, not a finalised one: CMS-6098-P (proposed 2026-11-16) would extrapolate Medicare Advantage RADV audit findings back to payment year 2018 and require insurers to remit improper payments. CMS estimates $90.2B of recoveries across the whole MA industry over 2027-2036. The comment period runs to 2027-01-19, so the overhang is months long and the de-rating it caused is the entry.
catalyst.action: Do not buy it here at 349.91 - wait. Accumulate in thirds only below 325.00, with the bulk near the 150-day low of 317.135, and add under 300.00 if the comment period produces worse headlines. This is a 12-24 month holding, not a bounce trade.

thesis: Four fetched quarters of actual EPS - 4.69, 6.38, 7.23 and 2.11 - sum to $20.41 trailing, so the 349.91 close is 17.1x and the 317.50 accumulation level is 15.6x. Against that, 897.59M shares means UNH alone shed $55.75B of market value in the two sessions from the 412.02 close of 2026-11-16, while the figure that caused it is CMS own estimate of $90.2B recovered from the entire Medicare Advantage industry across ten years. The target of 408.20 is simply 20x the EPS the company has already reported, a multiple it held two sessions ago.
key_risk: The rule is not the whole risk - the retroactivity is. Extrapolating audit findings to payment year 2018 creates a backward-looking liability UNH has not sized publicly, and until it does, the $90.2B industry estimate is the only number anyone has. The comment period closing 2027-01-19 means two more months in which worse drafts, state actions or political commentary can arrive with nothing to offset them, and there is no stop on this position by design.
counter_argument: The strongest bear case is that extrapolation to 2018 sticks, UNH turns out to be the most exposed plan because it is the largest, and the multiple de-rates to a regulated-utility 14x - which is the 285.74 bear price this idea is measured against, 18% below the close and below the 317.135 150-day low. The arithmetic answer: even if UNH were made to bear 100% of CMS own $90.2B industry-wide estimate, undiscounted, that is 1.6x what this one company lost in two trading sessions, spread over ten years. UNH is one of several MA plans, so its true share is a fraction of that. The market has priced a single-company outcome worse than the regulator asked the whole industry for.

thesis: Four fetched quarters of actual EPS - 2.09, 2.58, 2.57 and 1.09 - sum to $8.33 trailing, and CVS has beaten the estimate in all four. The 81.35 close is 9.77x and the 77.50 entry is 9.30x, against 17.14x for UNH on the same fetched-TTM method. Both are being sold on the same CMS proposal, and this one is already at 9.3x. The 108.29 target is 13.0x, a small discount to the 13.29x the stock itself carried at its 110.68 high inside the last 150 days, on earnings it has already reported rather than earnings it has to grow into.
key_risk: Two things the valuation does not answer, and they are why this is 2.5% and not larger. First, insiders are net sellers of $350,741,379 over six months - 8 sells against a single $2,001,315 purchase - and Glenview Capital was reported cutting its position into this selloff. Second, **this report already owned CVS and was stopped out of it on 2026-11-04**; buying it again 10% lower on a different horizon is a deliberate decision, not an oversight, and if it is wrong it will be wrong twice. EXPLICIT INVALIDATION (a price fall is not one): trailing-four-quarter reported EPS below $6.50 for two consecutive quarters, or CVS abandons the announced breakup, or it withdraws full-year guidance citing RADV liabilities. The 66.64 bear price is 8.0x trailing EPS, below the 9.14x the 150-day low of 76.10 represents.
counter_argument: The bear case is that CVS is the worst-placed name in the group, not the cheapest: Aetna carries the MA audit exposure, the planned breakup is unresolved, and the people who know the company best sold $350.7M of it. Answered with the only comparison that is measurable: CVS trades at 9.77x trailing EPS having beaten four of four quarters, while UNH, hit by the identical rule on the identical day, trades at 17.14x having beaten three of four. The audit risk is discounted roughly twice as hard here. The honest weakness is sensitivity - at a 12.5x target instead of 13.0x the reward-to-risk is 2.45 and this idea fails the 2.5 long-term floor outright. It survives on half a turn of multiple, and the red team should know that.

thesis: Pfizer has beaten the estimate in each of its last four reported quarters and the EPS series is rising through all four - 0.66, 0.75, 0.77, 0.87, up 31.8% from first to last - summing to $3.05 trailing. At the 28.06 close that is 9.20x. The amendment matters more than the thesis: the position was carrying a 42.00 target, which is 13.77x those earnings, against a 150-day high of 31.44 that is only 10.31x. A target a third above any multiple the stock has carried in the window is not a valuation anchor, and it is being cut to 36.60, or 12.0x.
key_risk: The real bear case here is the loss-of-exclusivity cliff and what replaces it, and I could not fetch pipeline, LOE schedule or segment revenue this morning - so the thesis rests on reported EPS and a multiple, with the part that actually decides the outcome unexamined. That is the honest limit of this idea and it is why conviction is 3. The sell side is cold too: bullish share 38.2% and deteriorating. EXPLICIT INVALIDATION (not a price move): trailing-four-quarter reported EPS falls below $2.40 - a 21% cut from the $3.05 reported - for two consecutive quarters, or Pfizer guides to a year-over-year revenue decline it does not attribute to a known patent expiry.
counter_argument: The case against is that 9.2x is not cheap for a company whose earnings are about to be taken away by patent expiries, and that a cheap multiple on peak earnings is a value trap - which is exactly the shape of the 0/4, -15.2% long-term record this report already has. It is not fully answered: I have the four quarters of rising EPS and the beats, and I do not have the LOE schedule to set against them. The 24.40 bear price, 8.0x trailing, is the acknowledgement - it sits just above the 7.74x that the 23.62 150-day low implies, so the downside case assumes the stock goes back to its worst multiple of the window.

thesis: Dycom is 60.1% below its 150-day high of 566.47 while beating the estimate in all four of its last four reported quarters - 3.63, 2.03, 4.42, 5.29, summing to $15.37 trailing, so the 225.78 close is 14.69x. The de-rating traces to one August guidance event in which roughly $150M of wireless program revenue was pushed into fiscal 2028 and a major wireless customer paused spending; in the same release full-year revenue guidance was raised to a $7.57B midpoint and total backlog grew 53% year-over-year to $12.24B. A timing shift in one segment, not a demand loss, is what 60% of the market value was taken for.
key_risk: The August print cut the stock 13% in a session on guidance alone, and 11/24 is the same kind of event with a 5.88% ATR behind it - a second deferral, or the wireless pause turning out to be a cancellation rather than a timing issue, gaps this straight through the 198.00 stop. Note also that Form 144 notices of intended sale were filed 2026-10-05 and 2026-11-05; no completed open-market sales appear in the six-month Form 4 record, but the intent is on file and that cuts against the insider-buying evidence below. Position is 2.5% rather than the 4-5% the evidence count would allow, deliberately.
counter_argument: The bear case is that this is a cyclical contractor whose largest customers are pausing capex, that fiber and wireless build cycles roll over hard, and that a 60% drawdown in a beating company usually means the market knows something the trailing numbers do not. It is answered, though with secondary sources rather than the transcript: the same August release that cut Q3 EPS guidance raised full-year revenue guidance to a $7.57B midpoint and reported backlog up 53% year-over-year to $12.24B, and an October investor letter described the wireless customer pause as timing while fiber-to-the-home and middle-mile demand stayed strong. Backlog up 53% is not the shape of a demand loss. The weaker part of the answer is that I did not read the 8-K or the transcript myself this morning.
